claims.text: A controlled high-temperature pre-oxidation step will form a continuous oxide scale on the refractory high-entropy alloy.
The pre-oxidation-induced oxide scale will be uniform and adherent.
The protective scale will be rich in alumina and/or chromia.
The pre-formed oxide scale will act as a diffusion barrier to oxygen.
The diffusion barrier will significantly reduce subsequent oxidation during prolonged high-temperature exposure.
Pre-oxidation selectively oxidizes reactive alloying elements such as Al and Cr at the alloy surface.
Al2O3 and Cr2O3 are thermodynamically stable protective oxides under the proposed conditions.
The protective scale limits oxygen ingress through both physical and chemical barrier effects.
At 1200 °C in 1 atm pure oxygen for 100 hours, pre-oxidized specimens will have a lower oxidation rate than untreated specimens.
After the specified exposure, pre-oxidized specimens will show less oxide-scale growth than untreated specimens.
After the specified exposure, pre-oxidized specimens will show lower weight gain than untreated specimens.
Performance at substantially different temperatures or oxygen partial pressures remains unestablished.
